- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes in history, then drop too sharply.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after mid-range or declining trends.
- Strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often overshoot downward after upward spikes, then fail to recover.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops, underestimating the depth of correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks downward adjustment mechanism.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast > true value by >5%, reduce by 10–15% for next period unless confirmed by new data.
- Avoid “overfitting to recent highs”: if last 5 days are rising, don’t assume continuation; cap forecast at 10% below recent peak.
